title: Electrician Website Builder: 5 Options and What They Cost
html:
An electrician website builder gets a basic site live in days, but it does not bring in calls. Wix, Squarespace, WordPress.com, Hostinger and Jimdo all let you build without a developer. Published builder prices here run from $0 to $40 a month.

An electrician website builder solves one problem: you need a site that looks credible and takes a call or a quote request. Homeowners check a website before they phone an electrician they found on a map. A slow, thin or broken site loses the call. This guide compares five builders with the price each vendor publishes and one real limit for each.

A builder gives you the tool and nothing else. You still write the pages, take the photos and keep the site fast.

Which electrician website builder is easiest to start with?

Wix and Squarespace are the two drag and drop builders an electrician is most likely to try first. Both come with templates, hosting and a free trial or free plan.

  • Wix: a drag and drop builder with hosting and templates. The source lists Light at $17.77 a month, Core at $29.77 and Business at $39.77. Those are yearly subscriptions paid in full, and prices vary by location. Limit: Light includes 2 GB of storage and 2 collaborators, so photo-heavy job galleries fill it fast.
  • Squarespace: a template builder with a 14 day free trial and no card needed. Basic has 2 contributors and charges a 2% fee on online store sales, while Core and Advanced list 0%. Limit: the page showed prices in a local currency, so check the vendor for your figure.

Wix gives you more control over layout. Squarespace gives you less freedom and cleaner templates. An electrician who dislikes fiddling should favor the template route, since fewer choices means fewer ways to break the page.

Ask both vendors what a domain and a mailbox cost, and total the first-year cost before you commit. A cheap plan with an expensive domain and mailbox can end up costing more than a mid-priced plan that bundles them.

Neither one needs the store features. Skip the store fees unless you plan to sell products. A service business needs a quote form, a phone number and a service list, and every plan covers those.

Which electrician website builder costs the least?

WordPress.com and Hostinger list the lowest prices in this guide, but both come with trade-offs in term length or setup effort.

  • WordPress.com: a hosted WordPress builder. Personal is $9 a month on monthly billing or $4 a month billed every 12 months. Premium is $18 monthly or $8 on a yearly term, and Business is $40 monthly or $25 on a yearly term. Limit: plugin installation starts on the Business plan, and a custom domain is free for one year only on annual and multi-year plans.
  • Hostinger Website Builder: Premium is listed at $1.99 a month. Unlimited is $2.79 and Cloud Startup is $7.99, each billed upfront for a 48 month term. Limit: renewal rates are higher, and Premium renews at $10.99 a month. Premium covers up to 3 websites and lists no ecommerce.

The Hostinger price needs a careful read. You pay the full 48 months at sign-up, so the first bill is $95.52 for Premium. The low monthly figure is real, but it is a long commitment, and the renewal is more than five times higher.

WordPress.com costs more per month on short terms but lets you change plans as you grow. Business adds plugin installs, which matters if you want a booking or quote tool later.

Is a free electrician website builder plan enough?

A free plan works as a test, not as a business site. It usually blocks a custom domain or shows the vendor's ads.

A subdomain such as a vendor name followed by your business name looks small on a van or a business card. A custom domain costs little and signals that you are a real company. Budget for a paid plan on day one.

How do the five electrician website builders compare?

The table puts the published facts side by side so you can see where each builder starts and where it stops.

BuilderPublished entry priceFree planMain limit
Wix$17.77 a month, yearly plan paid in fullYesLight has 2 GB storage
SquarespaceShown in local currency, check the vendor14 day trial2% store fee on Basic
WordPress.com$4 a month billed every 12 monthsYesNo plugins below Business
Hostinger$1.99 a month on a 48 month termNoPremium renews at $10.99
JimdoNot shown on the page read, check the vendorYesDomain renews at 26 euros

Source: the vendor's published prices, read in November 2026. Prices exclude tax unless the vendor says otherwise.

Read the table by goal. A quick test points to a free plan. A long-term cheap site points to Hostinger. A site you may grow into a booking tool points to WordPress.com Business.

What pages should an electrician website have?

An electrician website needs a page for each service, a service area page, proof of work and an easy way to call. Every builder above can make these pages.

  1. One page per service. Panel upgrades, rewiring, lighting and EV charger installs each deserve their own page and photos.
  2. A service area page. Name the cities you cover, so a homeowner knows you come to them.
  3. A phone number on every page. Make it a tap to call link on mobile.
  4. A short quote form. Ask for name, phone, address and job type, and nothing more.
  5. Real photos and reviews. Show finished work and quote customers who gave permission.
  6. License and insurance details. Show the credentials your state or province requires, since homeowners look for them.

Photos matter more than copy. A builder template with a hero photo of a real crew at work beats a stock image of a lightbulb. Take photos on every job, and add a few each month.

What should an electrician test during a builder trial?

Test the pages a homeowner uses on a phone, since most people searching for an electrician in a hurry are holding one.

  • Speed: load your trial site on a phone over mobile data and count how long the phone number takes to appear.
  • Call button: tap the number from a phone and confirm it dials without an extra step.
  • Form: send a test quote request and confirm it reaches your email and your phone.
  • Photos: upload ten job photos and check that the page still loads quickly.
  • Exit: find the export or cancel option, so you know how you would leave.

Ask a friend with an older phone to open the site. If the page is slow for them, it is slow for many of your customers. Fix that before you add more pages.

Check the cancel terms before you pay. A long upfront term, such as the 48 months on the Hostinger plans, is hard to undo. Read the refund wording and note the date you can still back out.

What does an electrician website builder not do?

A builder hosts pages. It does not rank them, write them or bring in homeowners, so a finished site still needs search and map work.

  • Google Business Profile: the free listing that puts an electrical company on Google Maps. Google states that creating a Business Profile and listing your business is free. Limit: it needs fresh photos and review replies to rank near the top.

Add electrician reputation management to turn finished jobs into reviews, and electrician SEO to help the site rank for each service.

Already own a site? Website management keeps it updated and fast.

When should an electrician pay for a managed build instead?

Choose a managed build when your time is worth more than the monthly fee and the site must produce calls, not just exist.

  • Do it yourself: you have a free weekend, a few photos and one service area. A builder at under $40 a month fits.
  • Managed build: you run several crews, serve many cities or want ranking work done for you. A professional build costs more, and a team manages the build.

That is a managed build, not a do it yourself builder, so it costs more than Wix or WordPress.com. The price covers design and build work you would otherwise do by hand.

Compare the cost with one average job. If a managed site wins one extra panel upgrade a quarter, the math changes. If you cannot say what a job is worth, find out before you choose either path.

How do you choose an electrician website builder?

Choose an electrician website builder with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every builder through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it let you add a page per service, a quote form and a tap to call button without code?

Cost: add the plan price, the domain, email and the renewal rate, then compare the total over three years.

Setup effort: can you publish a first version in a weekend, or will you stall on design choices?

A solo electrician can start on a Wix or Squarespace trial and a free Google Business Profile. A shop on a tight budget can price Hostinger or WordPress.com. A multi-crew company should price a managed build against the hours the owner would spend.

What is the best website builder for an electrician?

There is no single best, because it depends on budget and time. Wix and Squarespace are the easiest to start. WordPress.com suits a site that may grow. Hostinger lists the lowest monthly price. Try a trial and publish a real service page before you pay.

How much does an electrician website builder cost?

Published prices in this guide run from a free plan to $40 a month for WordPress.com Business on monthly billing. Hostinger Premium lists $1.99 a month on a 48 month term, and Wix Light lists $17.77. Domain, email and renewal rates cost more, so check each vendor.

Can an electrician build a site on a free plan?

You can, but free plans limit what you can do. WordPress.com Free gives a subdomain, no plugins and vendor ads. Most free plans block a custom domain. Use a free plan to test layouts, then move to a paid plan before you print the address on a truck.

Will a website builder get me more electrical leads?

No. A builder only hosts pages. Leads come from search, maps, reviews and ads. A fast site with a page for each service, a short quote form and a free Google Business Profile gives homeowners a reason to call you over a competitor.

When should an electrician hire a web team instead?

Hire a team when you serve many cities, run several crews or want ranking work done for you. A managed build costs more than a builder. It makes sense when one extra job a quarter would cover the difference, and you would rather spend your time on the truck.

How long does it take to build an electrician website?

A simple site with a home page, service pages and a quote form can go live in a weekend if you have photos ready. Writing a page for each service and collecting reviews takes longer, so plan a few weeks of steady additions.

When should an electrician hire a web team instead?
Hire a team when you serve many cities, run several crews or want ranking work done for you. A managed build costs more than a builder. It makes sense when one extra job a quarter would cover the difference, and you would rather spend your time on the truck.
###
How long does it take to build an electrician website?
A simple site with a home page, service pages and a quote form can go live in a weekend if you have photos ready. Writing a page for each service and collecting reviews takes longer, so plan a few weeks of steady additions.
